import Mathlib

/-!
# A Finite Ecosystem-Equilibrium Model of Theories

This file develops a small, completely finite, combinatorial optimization model of an
*ecosystem of theories*.  The picture is the following.

* A finite type `T` enumerates a collection of *theories* (or theory-states).
* Each theory carries three natural-number invariants:
  `connections t` (how many other theories it links to), `proofDensity t`
  (a coarse measure of how much is proved per unit of structure), and
  `axiomCount t` (the size of its axiomatic base, always positive).
* The *fitness* of a theory is the rational number
  `fitness t = (connections t * proofDensity t) / axiomCount t`:
  a theory is fitter when it is well connected and proof-dense relative to the
  number of assumptions it must postulate.
* A finite type `N` enumerates *ecological niches*.  A map `niche : T → N` assigns
  each theory to a niche.
* A finite set of theories `E` is *at equilibrium* (`AtEquilibrium E niche`) when
  distinct surviving theories occupy distinct niches, i.e. `niche` is injective on
  `E`.  This is the competitive-exclusion principle: two theories cannot stably
  coexist in the same niche.

The mathematical content is a clean finite optimization theory:

* **Well-definedness / positivity.**  The denominator `axiomCount t` is nonzero and
  `fitness` is always nonnegative.
* **Carrying capacity.**  An equilibrium set has at most `Fintype.card N` members
  (`card_le_card_niche`), and conversely any set larger than the number of niches
  cannot be at equilibrium (`not_atEquilibrium_of_card_lt`).
* **Aggregate fitness bounds.**  If every member of `E` clears a fitness threshold
  `q`, then the total fitness is at least `E.card • q`, and the *average* fitness is
  at least `q`.
* **Constructive niche selection.**  Given a candidate pool `C`, `selectByNiche`
  picks, in each occupied niche, the theory of maximal fitness.  The selected set is
  contained in `C`, is at equilibrium, has at most `Fintype.card N` members, and the
  chosen representative of a niche fitness-dominates every candidate in that niche.
* **Uniqueness under strict dominance.**  If each occupied niche has a *unique*
  fitness-maximizer, then `selectByNiche C niche` is the *only* equilibrium subset of
  `C` that occupies every occupied niche by a nichewise maximizer.

Everything is finite and is proved from standard `Finset`/`Fintype` cardinality
infrastructure.  No logarithms, entropy, or compression machinery is involved.
-/

namespace EcosystemEquilibrium

open scoped BigOperators
open Finset

variable {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
variable {N : Type*} [Fintype N] [DecidableEq N]

/-! ## Fitness -/

/-- The fitness of a theory: connectivity times proof-density per axiom. -/
def fitness (connections proofDensity axiomCount : T → ℕ) (t : T) : ℚ :=
  ((connections t : ℚ) * (proofDensity t : ℚ)) / (axiomCount t : ℚ)

variable {connections proofDensity axiomCount : T → ℕ}

omit [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] in
/-- The denominator of `fitness` is nonzero, given a positive axiom count. -/
lemma axiomCount_cast_ne_zero (hax : ∀ t, 0 < axiomCount t) (t : T) :
    (axiomCount t : ℚ) ≠ 0 := by
      exact Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr ( ne_of_gt ( hax t ) )

omit [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] in
/-- Fitness is always nonnegative. -/
lemma fitness_nonneg (t : T) : 0 ≤ fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount t := by
  exact div_nonneg ( mul_nonneg ( Nat.cast_nonneg _ ) ( Nat.cast_nonneg _ ) ) ( Nat.cast_nonneg _ )

/-! ## Equilibrium and carrying capacity -/

/-- A finite set of theories is *at equilibrium* when distinct surviving theories
occupy distinct niches: `niche` is injective on `E`. -/
def AtEquilibrium (E : Finset T) (niche : T → N) : Prop :=
  Set.InjOn niche (↑E : Set T)

omit [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] in
/-- Carrying capacity: an equilibrium set has at most as many members as there are
niches. -/
theorem card_le_card_niche {E : Finset T} {niche : T → N}
    (h : AtEquilibrium E niche) : E.card ≤ Fintype.card N := by
      exact Finset.card_le_card ( show E.image niche ⊆ Finset.univ from Finset.subset_univ _ ) |> le_trans ( by rw [ Finset.card_image_of_injOn h ] )

omit [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] in
/-- Pigeonhole converse: a set larger than the number of niches cannot be at
equilibrium. -/
theorem not_atEquilibrium_of_card_lt {E : Finset T} {niche : T → N}
    (h : Fintype.card N < E.card) : ¬ AtEquilibrium E niche :=
  fun he => absurd (card_le_card_niche he) (not_le.mpr h)

/-! ## Aggregate fitness bounds -/

omit [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] in
/-- If every member of `E` has fitness at least `q`, the total fitness is at least
`E.card • q`. -/
theorem card_nsmul_le_sum_fitness {E : Finset T} {q : ℚ}
    (h : ∀ t ∈ E, q ≤ fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount t) :
    E.card • q ≤ ∑ t ∈ E, fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount t :=
  Finset.card_nsmul_le_sum E _ q h

omit [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] in
/-- If every member of a nonempty `E` has fitness at least `q`, the *average*
fitness is at least `q`. -/
theorem le_avg_fitness {E : Finset T} {q : ℚ} (hE : E.Nonempty)
    (h : ∀ t ∈ E, q ≤ fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount t) :
    q ≤ (∑ t ∈ E, fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount t) / (E.card : ℚ) := by
  rw [ le_div_iff₀ ( Nat.cast_pos.mpr hE.card_pos ) ];
  simpa [ mul_comm ] using card_nsmul_le_sum_fitness h

/-! ## Constructive niche selection -/

/-- Candidates in pool `C` that live in niche `n`. -/
def nicheCandidates (C : Finset T) (niche : T → N) (n : N) : Finset T :=
  C.filter (fun t => niche t = n)

omit [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] [Fintype N] in
@[simp] lemma mem_nicheCandidates {C : Finset T} {niche : T → N} {n : N} {t : T} :
    t ∈ nicheCandidates C niche n ↔ t ∈ C ∧ niche t = n := by
  exact Finset.mem_filter

omit [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] [Fintype N] in
/-- The niche of any candidate `t ∈ C` is occupied: its own niche-candidate set is
nonempty. -/
lemma nicheCandidates_nonempty_self {C : Finset T} {niche : T → N} {t : T}
    (ht : t ∈ C) : (nicheCandidates C niche (niche t)).Nonempty :=
  ⟨t, mem_nicheCandidates.mpr ⟨ht, rfl⟩⟩

/-- The maximal-fitness representative of an occupied niche `n` in pool `C`. -/
noncomputable def nicheRepresentative (connections proofDensity axiomCount : T → ℕ)
    (C : Finset T) (niche : T → N) (n : N)
    (h : (nicheCandidates C niche n).Nonempty) : T :=
  Classical.choose (Finset.exists_max_image (nicheCandidates C niche n)
    (fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount) h)

omit [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] [Fintype N] in
lemma nicheRepresentative_mem {C : Finset T} {niche : T → N} {n : N}
    (h : (nicheCandidates C niche n).Nonempty) :
    nicheRepresentative connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche n h ∈
      nicheCandidates C niche n := by
  exact Classical.choose_spec ( Finset.exists_max_image _ _ h ) |>.1

omit [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] [Fintype N] in
lemma nicheRepresentative_max {C : Finset T} {niche : T → N} {n : N}
    (h : (nicheCandidates C niche n).Nonempty) :
    ∀ x ∈ nicheCandidates C niche n,
      fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount x ≤
        fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount
          (nicheRepresentative connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche n h) := by
  exact Classical.choose_spec ( Finset.exists_max_image _ _ h ) |>.2

omit [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] [Fintype N] in
/-- The representative of niche `n` indeed lies in `n`. -/
lemma nicheRepresentative_niche {C : Finset T} {niche : T → N} {n : N}
    (h : (nicheCandidates C niche n).Nonempty) :
    niche (nicheRepresentative connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche n h) = n :=
  (mem_nicheCandidates.mp (nicheRepresentative_mem h)).2

omit [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] [Fintype N] in
/-- The representative of niche `n` lies in the pool `C`. -/
lemma nicheRepresentative_mem_pool {C : Finset T} {niche : T → N} {n : N}
    (h : (nicheCandidates C niche n).Nonempty) :
    nicheRepresentative connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche n h ∈ C :=
  (mem_nicheCandidates.mp (nicheRepresentative_mem h)).1

/-- The selected ecosystem: one maximal-fitness representative per occupied niche. -/
noncomputable def selectByNiche (connections proofDensity axiomCount : T → ℕ)
    (C : Finset T) (niche : T → N) : Finset T :=
  C.attach.image (fun p =>
    nicheRepresentative connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche (niche p.1)
      (nicheCandidates_nonempty_self p.2))

omit [Fintype T] [Fintype N] in
/-- Every selected theory lies in the candidate pool. -/
theorem selectByNiche_subset {C : Finset T} {niche : T → N} :
    selectByNiche connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche ⊆ C := by
  intro y hy; rw [selectByNiche, Finset.mem_image] at hy; obtain ⟨p, _, rfl⟩ := hy; exact nicheRepresentative_mem_pool _;

omit [Fintype T] [Fintype N] in
/-- If `y` is selected, then it is the canonical representative of its own niche
(for any nonemptiness witness). -/
lemma selectByNiche_eq_rep {C : Finset T} {niche : T → N} {y : T}
    (hy : y ∈ selectByNiche connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche)
    (h : (nicheCandidates C niche (niche y)).Nonempty) :
    y = nicheRepresentative connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche (niche y) h := by
  obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ : ∃ p : C, nicheRepresentative connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche (niche p.1) (nicheCandidates_nonempty_self p.2) = y := by
    unfold selectByNiche at hy; aesop;
  grind +suggestions

omit [Fintype T] [Fintype N] in
/-- The niche of a selected theory is occupied in `C`. -/
lemma selectByNiche_niche_mem_image {C : Finset T} {niche : T → N} {y : T}
    (hy : y ∈ selectByNiche connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche) :
    niche y ∈ C.image niche := by
  convert Finset.mem_image_of_mem niche ( selectByNiche_subset hy ) using 1

omit [Fintype T] [Fintype N] in
/-- Selected theories occupy distinct niches: the selection is at equilibrium. -/
theorem atEquilibrium_selectByNiche {C : Finset T} {niche : T → N} :
    AtEquilibrium (selectByNiche connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche) niche := by
  intro a ha b hb hab;
  grind +locals

omit [Fintype T] in
/-- The selected ecosystem respects the carrying capacity. -/
theorem card_selectByNiche_le {C : Finset T} {niche : T → N} :
    (selectByNiche connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche).card ≤ Fintype.card N :=
  card_le_card_niche atEquilibrium_selectByNiche

omit [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] [Fintype N] in
/-- Optimality of the selection: in each occupied niche the chosen representative
fitness-dominates every candidate of that niche. -/
theorem fitness_le_representative {C : Finset T} {niche : T → N} {x : T} {n : N}
    (hx : x ∈ C) (hxn : niche x = n)
    (h : (nicheCandidates C niche n).Nonempty) :
    fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount x ≤
      fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount
        (nicheRepresentative connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche n h) :=
  nicheRepresentative_max h x (mem_nicheCandidates.mpr ⟨hx, hxn⟩)

omit [Fintype T] [Fintype N] in
/-- The chosen representative is itself selected. -/
theorem nicheRepresentative_mem_selectByNiche {C : Finset T} {niche : T → N} {n : N}
    (h : (nicheCandidates C niche n).Nonempty) :
    nicheRepresentative connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche n h ∈
      selectByNiche connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche := by
  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ : ∃ t, t ∈ nicheCandidates C niche n := by
    exact h;
  refine' Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨ ⟨ t, Finset.mem_filter.mp ht |>.1 ⟩, _, _ ⟩ <;> simp_all +decide [ nicheCandidates ];
  congr! 1;
  exact Finset.mem_filter.mp ht |>.2

/-! ## Uniqueness under strict dominance -/

/-- The hypothesis that within each niche of the pool `C` the fitness-maximizer is
unique: any two maximizers of the same niche coincide. -/
def UniqueNicheMaximizer (connections proofDensity axiomCount : T → ℕ)
    (C : Finset T) (niche : T → N) : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : N) (a b : T), a ∈ nicheCandidates C niche n → b ∈ nicheCandidates C niche n →
    (∀ s ∈ nicheCandidates C niche n,
      fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount s ≤ fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount a) →
    (∀ s ∈ nicheCandidates C niche n,
      fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount s ≤ fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount b) →
    a = b

omit [Fintype T] [Fintype N] in
/-- Uniqueness: under unique niche-maximizers, `selectByNiche C niche` is the only
equilibrium subset of `C` that covers every occupied niche with a nichewise
fitness-maximizer.

* `hsub : E ⊆ C` — survivors are drawn from the pool;
* `_heq : AtEquilibrium E niche` — the survivors form an equilibrium (this was part
  of the requested hypotheses; it is in fact logically redundant here, since the
  conclusion `E = selectByNiche ...` already forces equilibrium, so the proof does
  not use it);
* `hcover : E.image niche = C.image niche` — exactly the occupied niches are
  represented (one each, by the equilibrium condition);
* `hmax` — every survivor is a fitness-maximizer of its niche. -/
theorem eq_selectByNiche_of_unique {C E : Finset T} {niche : T → N}
    (huniq : UniqueNicheMaximizer connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche)
    (hsub : E ⊆ C)
    (_heq : AtEquilibrium E niche)
    (hcover : E.image niche = C.image niche)
    (hmax : ∀ e ∈ E, ∀ s ∈ nicheCandidates C niche (niche e),
      fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount s ≤
        fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount e) :
    E = selectByNiche connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche := by
  ext; simp [selectByNiche];
  constructor <;> intro h;
  · use ‹_›;
    exact ⟨ hsub h, huniq _ _ _ ( nicheRepresentative_mem _ ) ( by aesop ) ( nicheRepresentative_max _ ) ( hmax _ h ) ⟩;
  · obtain ⟨ a, ha, rfl ⟩ := h;
    obtain ⟨ e, he, he' ⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp ( hcover.symm ▸ Finset.mem_image_of_mem niche ha );
    have := huniq ( niche a ) e ( nicheRepresentative connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche ( niche a ) ( nicheCandidates_nonempty_self ha ) ) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ <;> simp_all +decide [ nicheCandidates ];
    · exact hsub he;
    · exact ⟨ nicheRepresentative_mem_pool _, nicheRepresentative_niche _ ⟩;
    · grind +suggestions

* **Paraconsistency (non-explosion).** With the designated set `D = {T, B}`, the
  "contradiction" premise `designated a ∧ designated (¬a)` is *satisfiable* in FOUR

  classical two-valued algebra makes that premise *unsatisfiable*, which is why classical
  logic is explosive.

  ("evidence-for", "evidence-against") is a bijection under which the knowledge order is
  the product order, the knowledge meet/join are componentwise `&&`/`||`, the truth order
  is the *twisted* product order (first up, second down), and negation is the coordinate
  swap. Hence FOUR has exactly `2² = 4` elements: it is the bilattice over the smallest
  non-trivial lattice `2 = Bool`.

-- !-- Lab Notebook -- !--

  and *valid* explosion — a gap that opens precisely when a value (here `B`) is both
  designated and has a designated negation. The fourth value `N` is forced as the

namespace BelnapFour
namespace Belnap

/-- The designated ("at least true") values: `T` and `B`. A valuation makes a sentence
assertible exactly when its value is designated. -/
def designated (a : Belnap) : Prop := a = T ∨ a = B

instance (a : Belnap) : Decidable (designated a) := by
  unfold designated; exact inferInstance

/-! ## Designation respects the truth order -/

-- !-- The truth order is the FDE entailment relation: moving up `≤_t` can only turn a
-- non-designated value designated, never the reverse. Finite case check. -- !--
/-- Tautological (FDE) entailment is the truth order: if `a ≤_t b` then designation is
preserved from `a` to `b`. -/
theorem tle_preserves_designated :
    ∀ a b : Belnap, tle a b → designated a → designated b := by
  decide

/-- **Theorem 4a.** The contradiction premise is *satisfiable* in FOUR: some value is

theorem explosion_premise_satisfiable :
    ∃ a : Belnap, designated a ∧ designated (neg a) := by
  decide

-- refutes explosion. Finite case check. -- !--
/-- **Theorem 4b (Paraconsistency).** FOUR is *non-explosive*: it is not the case that a

    ¬ (∀ a q : Belnap, designated a → designated (neg a) → designated q) := by
  decide

contradiction premise is unsatisfiable: no Boolean value is designated together with its
classical negation. -/

  decide

/-- The representation map sending a Belnap value to its
`(evidence-for, evidence-against)` pair in `Bool × Bool`. -/
def toProd : Belnap → Bool × Bool
  | N => (false, false)
  | F => (false, true)
  | T => (true, false)
  | B => (true, true)

/-- The inverse of `toProd`. -/

  | (false, true)  => F
  | (true, false)  => T

  invFun := ofProd
  left_inv a := belnap_iso_prod.1 a

coordinatewise Boolean operation on `Bool × Bool` (knowledge meet/join are componentwise
`&&`/`||`; truth meet/join twist the second coordinate; negation swaps; conflation
swap-negates). This is the defining property of the product bilattice `2 ⊙ 2`. -/

  on automatic sequences.
* `id_not_automatic` — the identity sequence `n ↦ n` is **not** `k`-automatic
  for any base `k`, because it has infinite range.  (We prove the strongest
  form, valid for every `k`, which in particular covers the requested `k ≥ 2`.)
* `DFAO.output_occurs_iff_reachable` — an output value `z` occurs among the
  outputs of some word iff some *reachable* state carries the label `z`.  This
  reduces an `∃`-over-words question to an `∃`-over-states question.
* `DFAO.output_occurs_bounded` / `DFAO.reachable_bounded_witness` — the
  pumping/shortest-path bound: anything reachable (resp. any achievable
  output) is reachable by a word of length **strictly less** than the number
  of states.  This is stated about *state reachability* (where it is true),
  not about representations of natural numbers (where it would be false).
* `DFAO.decEval` — combining the bounded witness with the finiteness of the
  alphabet, occurrence of an output is **decidable** by a finite search.
* `DFAO.unary_state_eventually_periodic` /
  `DFAO.unary_out_eventually_periodic` — for a fixed input letter `a`, the
  state sequence `n ↦ step^[n] start` and the output sequence
  `n ↦ out (step^[n] start)` are eventually periodic.  This uses the catalog
  theorem `eventually_periodic_of_finite` on iterates of a self-map of a
  finite type (from `MachineLearning.AdelicSync.Core`).

## Conventions

Base-`k` natural-number sequences are modelled by feeding the **little-endian**
digit list `Nat.digits k n` (Mathlib's convention) to the automaton.  The
finite-valuedness and non-automaticity results do not depend on the digit
convention or on leading-zero normalization: they hold for the value set of an
*arbitrary* encoding `repr : ℕ → List α`, so no false uniqueness-of-
representation assumption is used.
-/

namespace AutomaticSequences

universe u v w

variable {α : Type u} {σ : Type v} {β : Type w}

/-- A **deterministic finite automaton with output** (DFAO): a transition
function on states, an initial state, and an output labelling. -/
structure DFAO (α : Type u) (σ : Type v) (β : Type w) where
  /-- One-step transition: from state `s`, reading letter `a`, go to `step s a`. -/
  step : σ → α → σ
  /-- The initial state. -/
  start : σ
  /-- The output labelling of states. -/
  out : σ → β

namespace DFAO

/-- Run the automaton from state `s` over a word, processing left to right. -/
def run (M : DFAO α σ β) (s : σ) (w : List α) : σ := List.foldl M.step s w

/-- The output of the automaton on a word: the label of the final state when
started from `start`. -/
def eval (M : DFAO α σ β) (w : List α) : β := M.out (M.run M.start w)

@[simp] lemma run_nil (M : DFAO α σ β) (s : σ) : M.run s [] = s := rfl

@[simp] lemma run_cons (M : DFAO α σ β) (s : σ) (a : α) (w : List α) :
    M.run s (a :: w) = M.run (M.step s a) w := rfl

/-- Running over a concatenation is running over the first part, then the
second part starting from the intermediate state. -/
lemma run_append (M : DFAO α σ β) (s : σ) (a b : List α) :
    M.run s (a ++ b) = M.run (M.run s a) b := by
  simp [run, List.foldl_append]

/-- A state is **reachable** if some word leads to it from `start`. -/
def Reachable (M : DFAO α σ β) (s : σ) : Prop := ∃ w, M.run M.start w = s

/-- The base-`k` automatic sequence induced by a DFAO over the digit alphabet:
feed the little-endian base-`k` digits of `n`. -/
def autoSeq (M : DFAO ℕ σ β) (k : ℕ) (n : ℕ) : β := M.eval (Nat.digits k n)

/-! ## Finite-valuedness -/

/-- Every output of the automaton is the label of some state. -/
theorem eval_range_subset_out (M : DFAO α σ β) :
    Set.range M.eval ⊆ Set.range M.out := by
  rintro b ⟨w, rfl⟩
  exact ⟨M.run M.start w, rfl⟩

/-- A DFAO over a finite state type takes only finitely many values. -/
theorem eval_range_finite [Fintype σ] (M : DFAO α σ β) :
    (Set.range M.eval).Finite :=
  (Set.finite_range M.out).subset (eval_range_subset_out M)

/-- A base-`k` automatic sequence over finitely many states has finite range. -/
theorem autoSeq_range_finite [Fintype σ] (M : DFAO ℕ σ β) (k : ℕ) :
    (Set.range (M.autoSeq k)).Finite := by
  apply (eval_range_finite M).subset
  rintro b ⟨n, rfl⟩
  exact ⟨Nat.digits k n, rfl⟩

end DFAO

/-! ## Automaticity and the non-automaticity of `n ↦ n` -/

/-- A sequence `g : ℕ → β` is **`k`-automatic** if it is computed by some DFAO
over the base-`k` digit alphabet with finitely many states. -/
def IsKAutomatic (k : ℕ) (g : ℕ → β) : Prop :=
  ∃ (σ : Type) (_ : Fintype σ) (M : DFAO ℕ σ β), ∀ n, g n = M.autoSeq k n

/-- A `k`-automatic sequence has finite range. -/
theorem IsKAutomatic.range_finite {k : ℕ} {g : ℕ → β} (h : IsKAutomatic k g) :
    (Set.range g).Finite := by
  obtain ⟨σ, _, M, hM⟩ := h
  have hg : g = M.autoSeq k := funext hM
  rw [hg]
  exact DFAO.autoSeq_range_finite M k

/-- The identity sequence `n ↦ n` is **not** `k`-automatic for any base `k`
(in particular for every `k ≥ 2`), because its range is all of `ℕ`, which is
infinite, while automatic sequences have finite range. -/
theorem id_not_automatic (k : ℕ) : ¬ IsKAutomatic k (id : ℕ → ℕ) := by
  intro h
  have hfin := h.range_finite
  rw [Set.range_id] at hfin
  exact Set.infinite_univ hfin

namespace DFAO

/-! ## Output occurrence and reachability -/

/-- An output value `z` occurs among the outputs of some word **iff** some
reachable state carries the label `z`. -/
theorem output_occurs_iff_reachable (M : DFAO α σ β) (z : β) :
    (∃ w, M.eval w = z) ↔ ∃ s, M.Reachable s ∧ M.out s = z := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨w, hw⟩
    exact ⟨M.run M.start w, ⟨w, rfl⟩, hw⟩
  · rintro ⟨s, ⟨w, hw⟩, hz⟩
    refine ⟨w, ?_⟩
    rw [eval, hw]; exact hz

/-! ## Bounded (shortest-path) witnesses -/

/-
Pigeonhole / cycle-removal step: any word of length at least the number of
states can be shortened to a strictly shorter word reaching the **same** final
state.
-/
theorem exists_shorter_of_long [Fintype σ] (M : DFAO α σ β) (w : List α)
    (hlen : Fintype.card σ ≤ w.length) :
    ∃ w', M.run M.start w' = M.run M.start w ∧ w'.length < w.length := by
  obtain ⟨i, j, hij, h_eq⟩ : ∃ i j : Fin (w.length + 1), i < j ∧ M.run M.start (w.take i.val) = M.run M.start (w.take j.val) := by
    by_contra! h;
    exact absurd ( Fintype.card_le_of_injective ( fun i : Fin ( w.length + 1 ) => M.run M.start ( List.take i.val w ) ) fun i j hij => le_antisymm ( not_lt.1 fun hi => h _ _ hi hij.symm ) ( not_lt.1 fun hj => h _ _ hj hij ) ) ( by norm_num; linarith );
  refine' ⟨ w.take i.val ++ w.drop j.val, _, _ ⟩;
  · rw [ DFAO.run_append, h_eq, ← DFAO.run_append, List.take_append_drop ];
  · grind

/-
Shortest-path bound for state reachability: every word can be replaced by a
word reaching the same final state whose length is strictly less than the
number of states.
-/
theorem run_short_witness [Fintype σ] (M : DFAO α σ β) (w : List α) :
    ∃ w', M.run M.start w' = M.run M.start w ∧ w'.length < Fintype.card σ := by
  by_contra h;
  -- By induction on the length of the word w, we can show that there exists a shorter word w' such that M.run M.start w' = M.run M.start w and w'.length < Fintype.card σ.
  have h_ind : ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ w : List α, w.length = n → ∃ w' : List α, M.run M.start w' = M.run M.start w ∧ w'.length < Fintype.card σ := by
    intro n w hw;
    induction' n using Nat.strong_induction_on with n ih generalizing w;
    by_cases hlen : Fintype.card σ ≤ w.length;
    · obtain ⟨ w', hw' ⟩ := exists_shorter_of_long M w hlen;
      grind +revert;
    · exact ⟨ w, rfl, lt_of_not_ge hlen ⟩;
  exact h ( h_ind _ _ rfl )

/-- If a state is reachable at all, it is reachable by a word of length
strictly less than the number of states. -/
theorem reachable_bounded_witness [Fintype σ] (M : DFAO α σ β) (s : σ)
    (h : M.Reachable s) :
    ∃ w, M.run M.start w = s ∧ w.length < Fintype.card σ := by
  obtain ⟨w, rfl⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨w', hrun, hlen⟩ := run_short_witness M w
  exact ⟨w', hrun, hlen⟩

/-- If an output value `z` is achievable at all, it is achievable by a word of
length strictly less than the number of states. -/
theorem output_occurs_bounded [Fintype σ] (M : DFAO α σ β) (z : β)
    (h : ∃ w, M.eval w = z) :
    ∃ w, M.eval w = z ∧ w.length < Fintype.card σ := by
  obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨w', hrun, hlen⟩ := run_short_witness M w
  refine ⟨w', ?_, hlen⟩
  rw [eval, hrun]; exact hw

/-- Occurrence of an output value is **decidable**: by the bounded-witness
theorem it reduces to a finite search over words of length below the number of
states, of which there are finitely many when the alphabet is finite. -/
instance decEval [Fintype α] [Fintype σ] [DecidableEq β] (M : DFAO α σ β)
    (z : β) : Decidable (∃ w, M.eval w = z) :=
  decidable_of_iff
    (∃ n : Fin (Fintype.card σ), ∃ v : List.Vector α n.1, M.eval v.toList = z)
    (by
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨n, v, hv⟩
        exact ⟨v.toList, hv⟩
      · rintro ⟨w, hw⟩
        obtain ⟨w', hw', hlen⟩ := output_occurs_bounded M z ⟨w, hw⟩
        exact ⟨⟨w'.length, hlen⟩, ⟨w', rfl⟩, hw'⟩)

/-! ## Eventual periodicity in the unary case -/

/-- For a fixed input letter `a`, the state sequence `n ↦ step^[n] start` is
eventually periodic, by eventual periodicity of iterates of a self-map of a
finite type. -/
theorem unary_state_eventually_periodic [Fintype σ] [DecidableEq σ]
    (M : DFAO α σ β) (a : α) :
    IsEventuallyPeriodic (fun s => M.step s a) M.start :=
  eventually_periodic_of_finite _ _

/-
For a fixed input letter `a`, the **output** sequence
`n ↦ out (step^[n] start)` is eventually periodic: there are a preperiod `m`
and a period `n > 0` such that the outputs agree at `t` and `t + n` for all
`t ≥ m`.
-/
theorem unary_out_eventually_periodic [Fintype σ] [DecidableEq σ]
    (M : DFAO α σ β) (a : α) :
    ∃ m n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ ∀ t, m ≤ t →
      M.out ((fun s => M.step s a)^[t + n] M.start)
        = M.out ((fun s => M.step s a)^[t] M.start) := by
  obtain ⟨ m, n, h ⟩ := ( DFAO.unary_state_eventually_periodic M a );
  refine' ⟨ m, n, h.1, fun t ht => _ ⟩;
  convert congr_arg _ ( show ( fun s => M.step s a ) ^[ t + n ] M.start = ( fun s => M.step s a ) ^[ t ] M.start from ?_ ) using 1;
  induction ht <;> simp_all +decide [ Nat.succ_add, Function.iterate_succ_apply' ]

end DFAO

end AutomaticSequences

# Future Directions — Automatic Sequences and the Zero-in-Sequence Problem

This cycle formalized the automata-theoretic core of the "halting problem for
automatic sequences": the zero-in-sequence problem reduces to DFA language
emptiness, which a pumping/pigeonhole argument collapses to a *finite* search
(`accepts_nonempty_iff_short`, `zero_value_iff_short`), with the companion
infinitude dichotomy (`accepts_infinite_of_long`, `zero_value_infinite`).  We
also pinned the boundary with `P`-recursive sequences: automatic sequences are
finite-valued (`autoSeq_range_finite`), so `a_n = n` is *not* automatic
(`id_not_automatic`), and unary automatic sequences are eventually periodic
(`unary_autoSeq_eventually_periodic`, built on the catalog's
`pow_eventually_periodic`).

The conjectures below are derived directly from those findings.

## C1. Sharp pumping threshold for the zero set is exactly the state count
**Conjecture.** For a DFAO with `s` states and output map `out`, the set
`{w | out (M.eval w) = z}` is infinite **iff** it contains a word of length in the
window `[s, 2s)`; equivalently, finiteness is decided by inspecting words of
length `< s` only, and infinitude by exhibiting one in `[s, 2s)`.

**The key insight is** that `DFA.pumping_lemma` already localizes the loop `b`
inside the first `s` letters (`a.length + b.length ≤ s`), so the entire
finite/infinite dichotomy is witnessed within a bounded length window rather than
unboundedly far out.

**Why now?** We have machine-checked both halves of the dichotomy
(`accepts_finite_iff` and `accepts_infinite_of_long`); tightening the witness
length from "≥ s" to the explicit window `[s, 2s)` is a finite combinatorial
refinement that our existing pumping infrastructure should discharge.

## C2. Eventual periodicity generalizes from unary to ultimately-constant inputs
**Conjecture.** If the representation stream `repr n` is eventually constant in
its tail letter (reads a fixed letter `a` after a bounded prefix), then
`n ↦ out (M.eval (repr n))` is eventually periodic, with period dividing the
order of `s ↦ M.step s a` in `Function.End σ`.

**The key insight is** that `unary_autoSeq_eventually_periodic` already shows the
tail dynamics are governed by a single endofunction's orbit; a bounded prefix only
shifts the starting state, leaving the eventual period intact.

**Why now?** `End_pow_apply` + `evalFrom_replicate` give an exact bridge between
list evaluation and monoid powers, so the prefix-shift argument is within reach of
the same `pow_eventually_periodic` engine we already invoked.

## C3. Finite-valuedness is the decisive separator: automatic ⊊ P-recursive
**Conjecture.** Every `k`-automatic integer sequence is `P`-recursive, but the
converse fails on exactly the unbounded `P`-recursive sequences; a `P`-recursive
sequence is automatic only if it takes finitely many values.

**The key insight is** that `autoSeq_range_finite` makes finite range a *necessary*
condition for automaticity, and `id_not_automatic` shows the simplest unbounded
`P`-recursive sequence `a_n = n` already violates it — so the boundary is "bounded
range", not the degree of the recurrence as the original conjecture claimed.

**Why now?** We have a formal, axiom-clean obstruction (`autoSeq_range_finite`);
the remaining task is to formalize the `automatic ⟹ P-recursive` direction and the
finite-range converse, both of which are structural rather than analytic.

## C4. Decidability survives the morphic boundary for *length-uniform* morphisms
**Conjecture.** The zero-in-sequence problem stays decidable for morphic
sequences generated by morphisms whose iterated images have lengths obeying a
linear recurrence (a strict subclass of general morphic sequences), via a pumping
argument on the substitution graph rather than the DFA.

**The key insight is** that the DFA pumping argument we formalized only used
finiteness of the state set plus a loop; a length-uniform morphism induces a
finite "block automaton" whose loops admit the same down-pump/up-pump dichotomy.

**Why now?** The reusable lemmas `exists_shorter_of_long` and
`accepts_infinite_of_long` are stated abstractly over any DFA, so porting them to
the block automaton of a length-uniform morphism is a definitional, not
foundational, step — letting us probe precisely where decidability breaks toward
the general (open) morphic case.

## C5. The decidable instance is a certified bounded-search algorithm
**Conjecture.** `decidableExistsOutputValue` extracts (via `Decidable.decide`) a
total algorithm that, on any explicitly presented DFAO over a finite alphabet,
returns a witness word of length `< s` whenever the value `z` is attainable, and a
proof of non-attainability otherwise — and this is *optimal* in worst-case search
depth.

**The key insight is** that `zero_value_iff_short` certifies correctness of the
bounded search and `accepts_infinite_of_long` certifies that no shorter universal
bound than `s` exists, so the instance is not just decidable but length-optimal.

**Why now?** The `Decidable` instance is already machine-checked; turning it into a
benchmarked, extracted decision procedure (the mission's "verify on 100 test
sequences" test) is now purely an engineering exercise on top of verified math.

import Mathlib

/-!
# EML Special Functions I — The Gamma function as a meromorphic EML function

This file is part of the *EML Special Functions* research cycle (Gamma, Zeta,
Hypergeometric).  The catalog's `EML` subtree studies the class of functions
built from `exp`, `log`, multiplication and affine maps (see
`Catalog/EML/KolmogorovArnoldEMLDeep.lean`).  Here we study the genuine
analytic object closest to that class on the complex plane: the
**Gamma function** `Γ`.

## Mission claim and what we actually prove

The research mission asks us to show that `Γ(z)` is a *meromorphic EML function*
that "has no algebraic singularities".  We make this precise and prove it:

* `gamma_meromorphic` — `Γ` is meromorphic on all of `ℂ`.
* `gamma_recip_entire` — the reciprocal `1/Γ` is **entire** (differentiable
  everywhere).  This is the decisive form of *"no algebraic singularities"*:
  a function whose reciprocal is entire can only have poles, never branch
  points or essential singularities.
* `gamma_recip_vanishes_at_poles` — `1/Γ` vanishes at exactly the pole locations
  `-n`, confirming that the poles are simple zeros of the entire reciprocal.
* `gamma_infinitely_many_poles` — `Γ` fails to be continuous at every
  non-positive integer, so it has *infinitely many* poles (contrast this with
  the zeta function, which has a single pole — see `ZetaEML.lean`).
* `gamma_no_zeros` — `Γ` has no zeros away from its poles.
* `gamma_extends_factorial` — `Γ` interpolates the factorial.

namespace TransfiniteCABridge

variable {ι : Type*}

/-- An **ordinal Lyapunov potential** for a local rule `step`: the potential strictly drops
whenever the rule actually changes the configuration. -/
def LyapunovPotential (step : Cfg ι → Cfg ι) (pot : Cfg ι → Ordinal) : Prop :=
  ∀ c, step c ≠ c → pot (step c) < pot c

variable {step : Cfg ι → Cfg ι} {pot : Cfg ι → Ordinal}

/-- A Lyapunov potential never increases under `step`. -/
theorem pot_step_le (h : LyapunovPotential step pot) (c : Cfg ι) :
    pot (step c) ≤ pot c := by
  by_cases hc : step c = c
  · rw [hc]
  · exact (h c hc).le

/-- The potential along the finite orbit is a non-increasing `ℕ → Ordinal` sequence. -/
theorem pot_orbit_noninc (h : LyapunovPotential step pot) (init : Cfg ι) (n : ℕ) :
    pot (step^[n + 1] init) ≤ pot (step^[n] init) := by
  rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply']
  exact pot_step_le h _

the non-increasing potential to `Ordinal.nonincreasing_eventually_constant` and then uses the

theorem wellfounded_reaches_fixed (h : LyapunovPotential step pot) (init : Cfg ι) :
    ∃ N : ℕ, step (step^[N] init) = step^[N] init := by
  obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := Ordinal.nonincreasing_eventually_constant
    (fun n => pot (step^[n] init)) (pot_orbit_noninc h init)
  refine ⟨N, ?_⟩
  by_contra hne
  -- if the configuration still changes, the potential strictly drops, contradicting `hN`.
  have hlt : pot (step^[N + 1] init) < pot (step^[N] init) := by
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply']
    exact h _ hne
  have heq : pot (step^[N + 1] init) = pot (step^[N] init) := hN (N + 1) (Nat.le_succ N)
  exact absurd heq (ne_of_lt hlt)

    (hfix : step (step^[N] init) = step^[N] init) :
    ∀ m : ℕ, step^[N + m] init = step^[N] init := by
  intro m
  induction m with
  | zero => simp
  | succ k ih =>
    rw [show N + (k + 1) = (N + k) + 1 from by ring, Function.iterate_succ_apply', ih, hfix]

    ¬ IsGardenOfEden step (step^[N] init) := by
  intro hG
  exact hG (step^[N] init) hfix

produced.  Compare `ittm_toggle_super_turing`, where no ordinal potential exists and the `ω`

    (hfix : step (step^[N] init) = step^[N] init) :
    (ittmCA step).run init ω = step^[N] init := by
  funext i
  -- past `N` the orbit is constant, so the `limsup` reduces to the fixed cell value.
  have hconst : ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n → (step^[n] init) i = (step^[N] init) i := by
    intro n hn
    obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hn
    rw [orbit_const_after init hfix m]
  have key : (∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (step^[n] init) i = true) ↔ (step^[N] init) i = true := by
    constructor
    · intro hf
      obtain ⟨n, hn, hval⟩ := (Filter.frequently_atTop.mp hf) N
      rw [← hconst n hn]; exact hval
    · intro hval
      rw [Filter.frequently_atTop]
      intro a
      refine ⟨max a N, le_max_left _ _, ?_⟩
      rw [hconst (max a N) (le_max_right _ _)]; exact hval
  have hiff := ittm_run_omega step init i
  rw [key] at hiff
  cases hr : (ittmCA step).run init ω i <;> cases hc : (step^[N] init) i <;>

      | rfl
      | (rw [hr, hc] at hiff; simp at hiff)

/-- **Flagship bridge theorem.**  For a transfinite cellular automaton carrying an ordinal
Lyapunov potential there is a finite stage `N` whose configuration `c = step^[N] init`
simultaneously
  * is a genuine fixed point (`step c = c`),
  * is **not** a Garden-of-Eden state, and
  * equals the transfinite `ω`-evolution `(ittmCA step).run init ω`.

attractor and renders the transfinite clock (Shared) redundant — three catalog domains
combined into one statement. -/
theorem wellfounded_transfinite_ca_collapses (h : LyapunovPotential step pot) (init : Cfg ι) :
    ∃ N : ℕ,
      step (step^[N] init) = step^[N] init ∧
      ¬ IsGardenOfEden step (step^[N] init) ∧
      (ittmCA step).run init ω = step^[N] init := by
  obtain ⟨N, hfix⟩ := wellfounded_reaches_fixed h init
  exact ⟨N, hfix, fixed_not_gardenOfEden hfix, wellfounded_omega_eq_fixed init hfix⟩

end TransfiniteCABridge

import Mathlib

open Ordinal Filter
open scoped Classical

namespace TransfiniteCA

/-- A configuration assigns a Boolean to each cell of the space `ι`. -/
abbrev Cfg (ι : Type*) := ι → Bool

/-- A **transfinite cellular automaton** over the cell space `ι`: a local `step` rule used at
successor stages, and a global `lim` rule used at limit stages (reading the entire preceding
history of configurations). -/
structure _root_.TransfiniteCA (ι : Type*) where
  /-- Local update applied at every successor stage. -/
  step : Cfg ι → Cfg ι
  /-- Global rule applied at every limit stage to the history below it. -/
  lim  : (Ordinal → Cfg ι) → Cfg ι

variable {ι : Type*}

/-- The transfinite evolution of `M` from `init`, indexed by the ordinals, defined by
transfinite recursion: `init` at `0`, `step` at successors, and `lim` of the history at
limits. -/
noncomputable def run (M : TransfiniteCA ι) (init : Cfg ι) (o : Ordinal) : Cfg ι :=
  Ordinal.limitRecOn o init (fun _ ih => M.step ih)
    (fun o _ ih => M.lim (fun p => if h : p < o then ih p h else init))

@[simp] theorem run_zero (M : TransfiniteCA ι) (init : Cfg ι) : M.run init 0 = init := by
  unfold run; rw [Ordinal.limitRecOn_zero]

@[simp] theorem run_succ (M : TransfiniteCA ι) (init : Cfg ι) (o : Ordinal) :
    M.run init (Order.succ o) = M.step (M.run init o) := by
  unfold run; rw [Ordinal.limitRecOn_succ]

/-- On the natural numbers the transfinite evolution is just finite iteration of `step`. -/
theorem run_natCast (M : TransfiniteCA ι) (init : Cfg ι) (n : ℕ) :
    M.run init (n : Ordinal) = (M.step^[n]) init := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ k ih =>
    have : ((k + 1 : ℕ) : Ordinal) = Order.succ (k : Ordinal) := by
      rw [Nat.cast_succ]; exact Ordinal.add_one_eq_succ _
    rw [this, run_succ, ih, Function.iterate_succ_apply']

/-- At a limit stage the evolution is the global rule applied to the preceding history. -/
theorem run_limit (M : TransfiniteCA ι) (init : Cfg ι) {o : Ordinal}
    (ho : Order.IsSuccLimit o) :
    M.run init o = M.lim (fun p => if p < o then M.run init p else init) := by
  unfold run
  rw [Ordinal.limitRecOn_limit _ _ _ _ ho]
  simp only [dite_eq_ite]

/-- Past the first limit, finite iteration resumes: stage `ω + n` is `n` `step`s after `ω`. -/
theorem run_omega_add_nat (M : TransfiniteCA ι) (init : Cfg ι) (n : ℕ) :
    M.run init (ω + n) = (M.step^[n]) (M.run init ω) := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ k ih =>
    have : (ω + (k + 1 : ℕ)) = Order.succ (ω + (k : ℕ)) := by
      push_cast; rw [← add_assoc]; exact Ordinal.add_one_eq_succ _
    rw [this, run_succ, ih, Function.iterate_succ_apply']

/-- The **ITTM limit rule**: at a limit stage a cell is on iff it is on *cofinally often*
(`limsup`) along the natural-number stages of the history below. -/
noncomputable def ittmLim (h : Ordinal → Cfg ι) : Cfg ι :=
  fun i => if (∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, h (n : Ordinal) i = true) then true else false

/-- The transfinite CA driven by a local rule with the ITTM limit law. -/
noncomputable def ittmCA (step : Cfg ι → Cfg ι) : TransfiniteCA ι := ⟨step, ittmLim⟩

theorem ittmLim_apply (h : Ordinal → Cfg ι) (i : ι) :
    ittmLim h i = true ↔ ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, h (n : Ordinal) i = true := by
  unfold ittmLim
  by_cases hc : (∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, h (n : Ordinal) i = true) <;> simp [hc]

/-- **ITTM limit law inside a cellular automaton.**  The cell value at stage `ω` is `true`
iff that cell is on cofinally often (the `limsup`) during the finite evolution. -/
theorem ittm_run_omega (step : Cfg ι → Cfg ι) (init : Cfg ι) (i : ι) :
    (ittmCA step).run init ω i = true ↔ ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (step^[n] init) i = true := by
  rw [run_limit _ _ isSuccLimit_omega0]
  rw [show (ittmCA step).lim = ittmLim from rfl, ittmLim_apply]
  apply Filter.frequently_congr
  filter_upwards with n
  rw [if_pos (nat_lt_omega0 n), run_natCast]
  rfl

changing finitely many stages cannot affect it. -/
theorem ittmLim_tail_invariant (h1 h2 : Ordinal → Cfg ι) (i : ι) (N : ℕ)
    (htail : ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n → h1 (n : Ordinal) i = h2 (n : Ordinal) i) :
    ittmLim h1 i = ittmLim h2 i := by
  unfold ittmLim
  congr 1
  apply propext
  apply Filter.frequently_congr
  rw [Filter.eventually_atTop]
  exact ⟨N, fun n hn => by rw [htail n hn]⟩

/-- **The limit rule is not finitary (super-Turing separation).**  For every finite stage
`N` there is a history whose ITTM `ω`-value differs from its value at stage `N`.  Hence no
finite truncation reproduces the transfinite limit. -/
theorem ittmLim_not_finitary (N : ℕ) :
    ∃ h : Ordinal → Cfg Unit, ittmLim h () ≠ h (N : Ordinal) () := by
  refine ⟨fun o _ => if o = (N : Ordinal) then false else true, ?_⟩
  have hfreq : ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (if (n : Ordinal) = (N : Ordinal) then false else true) = true := by
    rw [Filter.frequently_atTop]
    intro a
    refine ⟨a + N + 1, by omega, ?_⟩
    have hne : ((a + N + 1 : ℕ) : Ordinal) ≠ (N : Ordinal) := by
      rw [Ne, Nat.cast_inj]; omega
    rw [if_neg hne]
  have h1 : ittmLim (fun o (_ : Unit) => if o = (N : Ordinal) then false else true) () = true := by
    unfold ittmLim; rw [if_pos hfreq]
  rw [h1]; simp

/-! ## A concrete super-Turing witness: the parity (local-flip) automaton -/

/-- The **parity / local-flip automaton** on a single cell: each successor step flips the
cell.  Its finite orbit `false, true, false, true, …` never converges. -/
def toggleStep : Cfg Unit → Cfg Unit := fun c _ => !(c ())

/-- Closed form of the parity orbit: cell on at finite stage `n` iff `n` is odd. -/
theorem toggle_orbit (n : ℕ) :
    (toggleStep^[n] (fun _ => false)) () = decide (Odd n) := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ k ih =>
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply']
    simp only [toggleStep]
    rw [ih]
    simp only [Nat.odd_add_one]
    by_cases h : Odd k <;> simp [h]

/-- The parity orbit is on cofinally often. -/
theorem toggle_freq_true :
    ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (toggleStep^[n] (fun _ => false)) () = true := by
  rw [Filter.frequently_atTop]; intro a
  exact ⟨2 * a + 1, by omega, by
    rw [toggle_orbit]; simp only [decide_eq_true_eq]; exact ⟨a, by ring⟩⟩

/-- The parity orbit is off cofinally often. -/
theorem toggle_freq_false :
    ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (toggleStep^[n] (fun _ => false)) () = false := by
  rw [Filter.frequently_atTop]; intro a
  refine ⟨2 * a + 2, by omega, ?_⟩
  rw [toggle_orbit]
  simp only [decide_eq_false_iff_not, Nat.not_odd_iff_even]
  exact ⟨a + 1, by ring⟩

(cofinally on **and** cofinally off, so no finite-time machine assigns it a stable value),
yet the transfinite machine assigns it the definite value `true` at stage `ω`.  The
transfinite limit decides a `limsup` that no finite computation can. -/
theorem ittm_toggle_super_turing :
    (∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (toggleStep^[n] (fun _ => false)) () = true) ∧
    (∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (toggleStep^[n] (fun _ => false)) () = false) ∧
    (ittmCA toggleStep).run (fun _ => false) ω () = true := by
  refine ⟨toggle_freq_true, toggle_freq_false, ?_⟩
  rw [ittm_run_omega]
  exact toggle_freq_true

/-! ## Why `ω²`: cofinally many nested limit stages -/

/-- Each `ω·(k+1)` is a genuine limit stage strictly below `ω²`. -/
theorem omega_mul_succ_limit (k : ℕ) :
    Order.IsSuccLimit (ω * ((k : Ordinal) + 1)) ∧ ω * ((k : Ordinal) + 1) < ω ^ 2 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [mul_add, mul_one]
    exact Ordinal.isSuccLimit_add _ isSuccLimit_omega0
  · rw [pow_two]
    exact mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left (by exact_mod_cast nat_lt_omega0 (k + 1)) omega0_pos

stages `ω·(k+1)`, each carrying its own ITTM limit.  Thus an `ω²` computation stacks
infinitely many transfinite limits — transfinite computation of transfinite computations —
which a single `ω`-limit cannot provide. -/
theorem omega_sq_has_infinitely_many_limit_stages :
    ∀ B : Ordinal, B < ω ^ 2 → ∃ q, B < q ∧ q < ω ^ 2 ∧ Order.IsSuccLimit q := by
  intro B hB
  -- `ω·(k+1)` grows without bound below `ω²`, so some such limit stage exceeds `B`.
  obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ : ∃ k : ℕ, B < ω * ((k : Ordinal) + 1) := by
    have hdivlt : B / ω < ω := by
      rw [Ordinal.div_lt omega0_pos.ne']; rw [← pow_two]; exact hB
    obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := Ordinal.lt_omega0.mp hdivlt
    refine ⟨k, ?_⟩
    have hmod : B % ω < ω := Ordinal.mod_lt B omega0_pos.ne'
    calc B = ω * (B / ω) + B % ω := (Ordinal.div_add_mod B ω).symm
      _ < ω * (B / ω) + ω := add_lt_add_right hmod _
      _ = ω * (B / ω + 1) := by rw [mul_add, mul_one]
      _ = ω * ((k : Ordinal) + 1) := by rw [hk]
  refine ⟨ω * ((k : Ordinal) + 1), hk, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [pow_two]
    exact mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left (by exact_mod_cast nat_lt_omega0 (k + 1)) omega0_pos
  · rw [mul_add, mul_one]
    exact Ordinal.isSuccLimit_add _ isSuccLimit_omega0

concept.title: Langlands for Toddlers: Galois Groups as Shapes, Automorphic Forms as Colors
concept.concept_description: The Langlands program connects Galois groups (shapes) to automorphic forms (colors). Think of it this way: a Galois group is the group of symmetries of a shape (like the rotational symmetries of a polygon). An automorphic form is a coloring that respects the shape's symmetries (like a coloring of the polygon's vertices that is invariant under rotation). The Langlands correspondence says: for every 'shape' (Galois representation), there is a matching 'color' (automorphic form) and vice versa. Conjecture: This correspondence is a bijection between irreducible representations of Gal(Q_bar/Q) and cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n over Q. For n=1, this is class field theory (every abelian extension of Q corresponds to a Dirichlet character). For n=2, this is the modularity theorem (every elliptic curve over Q corresponds to a weight-2 cusp form). The toddler version: each shape has exactly one matching color, and each color has exactly one matching shape. Test: verify the correspondence for all degree-2 extensions of Q up to discriminant 1000. Verify that each quadratic field Q(sqrt(d)) corresponds to a Dirichlet character chi_d via the correspondence chi_d(p) = (d/p) (Legendre symbol). Impact: Langlands is just shape-color matching. Shapes and colors are two ways of seeing the same mathematical object.
